purpose: This medication is an antibiotic used to treat urinary tract infections (UTIs) — those uncomfortable bladder infections that cause burning, frequent urination, and pain. It works specifically in the urinary tract and is not used for infections in other parts of the body. Your doctor may also prescribe it to help prevent UTIs if you get them frequently.
how_it_works: Nitrofurantoin works by getting absorbed into the bacteria that are causing your UTI and damaging their DNA, which stops them from growing and kills them off. Because this medication concentrates mainly in your urine, it is very effective right where the infection is happening — in your bladder and urinary tract. Think of it as a targeted antibiotic that goes straight to the source of the problem.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, upset stomach, vomiting, and diarrhea — taking it with food usually helps a lot. You may also notice your urine turning dark yellow or brown, which is completely harmless and normal. Some people experience mild headache or dizziness as well.
warnings: Stop taking this medication and contact your doctor right away if you develop shortness of breath, chest pain, persistent cough, or yellowing of your skin or eyes, as these could be signs of rare but serious lung or liver problems. Do not take this medication if you have significant kidney disease, as it may not work properly and could build up to harmful levels. Avoid this medication if you are near the end of pregnancy (38-42 weeks). Always finish your full course of antibiotics even if you feel better, so the infection does not come back.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose for treating a UTI is one 100 mg capsule taken twice a day (every 12 hours) for 5 to 7 days. Always take it with food or milk to reduce stomach upset and to help your body absorb it better. If you are taking it to prevent UTIs, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose taken once daily, often at bedtime.
